title: Biomedical research in  Psychiatric Disorders (biomedicine)

held_out_paper.citation: Comprehensive functional genomic resource and integrative model for the human brain

ground_truth_hypothesis: For the research problem 'Biomedical research in  Psychiatric Disorders', the held-out later work (Comprehensive functional genomic resource and integrative model for the human brain) established: Used models: Deep structured phenotype network (DSPN); Findings: The model provided insights about intermediate phenotypes and their connections to high-level phenotypes (disease traits).; Study cohort: PsychENCODE Consortium dataset g

prior_literature.title: Mood disorder identification using deep bottleneck features of elicited speech
claims: Findings: The denoising autoencoder adopted emotion domain data to the speech data space to generate emotion profiles (EPs). The LSTM characterized the temporal evolution of the EP sequence with respect to eliciting emotional videos.
Study cohort: 15 BDs, 15 UDs, and 15 HCs (Chi-Mei mood dataset)

prior_literature.title: Exploring microscopic fluctuation of facial expression for mood disorder classification
claims: Findings: The study modeled the longterm variation among different mood disorders types by LSTM.
Study cohort: 12 BDs, 12 MDDs, and 12 HCs (Chi-Mei mood dataset)

prior_literature.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
claims: Used models: Facial expression RGBD data
Findings: The study established the relationship between facial expression/gestures and neurodevelopmental conditions such as ADHD and ASD.
Study cohort: 4 ADHDs, 22 ASDs, 11 ADHD +ASDs, and 18 HCs
performance: ACC= 0.96 (condition vs. HC) and 0.93 (ADHD + ASD vs. ASD only)
Aim: Prediction of ADHD and ASD

prior_literature.title: DeepBreath: Deep learning of breathing patterns for automatic stress recognition using low-cost thermal imaging in unconstrained settings
claims: Findings: The model identified psychological stress level by using a low-cost thermal camera, which tracks the person’s breathing patterns.
performance: ACC= 0.846 (no stress vs. stress) and 0.565 (no stress vs. low-level stress vs. high-level stress)

prior_literature.title: DCNN and DNN based multi-modal depression recognition
claims: Findings: The study proposed a multimodal approach: two CNNs were introduced to encode audio and video data, respectively. Then a fully connected DNN was used to combine the two channel feature maps to predict PHQ-8 scores.
Study cohort: 189 Segments of clinical interview (AVEC dataset)

prior_literature.title: An Affect Prediction Approach Through Depression Severity Parameter Incorporation in Neural Networks
claims: Findings: The DFNN incorporated depression severity as the parameter, linking the effects of depression on subjects’ affective expressions.
Outcome assessment: dominance ratings by human annotation

prior_literature.title: Characterisation of mental health conditions in social media using Informed Deep Learning
claims: Findings: (1) The most common misclassification is depression; (2) Some of the themes are highly inter-related and not always distinguishable as separate and exclusive classes.
Study cohort: 538,245 Posts related to 11 mental themes, 476,388 non-mental health postsi

prior_literature.title: Correlating Stressor Events for Social Network Based Adolescent Stress Prediction
claims: Findings: The model incorporated relationships of stressor events and improved the prediction of stress in adolescent.
Study cohort: 29,232 Posts of 124 students, containing 122 study-related stressor events

prior_literature.title: Detecting Stress Based on Social Interactions in Social Networks
claims: Findings: Users stress state is closely related to that of his/her friends in social media.
Outcome assessment: Pattern matching in tweets
Study cohort: 11,074 Subjects of stress, 12,230 subjects of no stress

claims: Findings: The RNN captured sequential information from texts with sequential property.
